import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
sns.set_palette("viridis")

# Create a figure with three subplots arranged in a row
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(20, 6))

# --- Plot 1: Distribution of Transaction Amounts for Fraudulent vs. Non-Fraudulent ---
sns.boxplot(x='is_fraud', y='amount', data=df, ax=axes[0])
axes[0].set_title('Transaction Amount by Fraud Status', fontsize=14, weight='bold')
axes[0].set_yscale('log')  # Use log scale due to skewed amount data
axes[0].set_xlabel('Is Fraudulent', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Transaction Amount (Log Scale)', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_xticklabels(['No', 'Yes'])

# --- Plot 2: Count of Fraudulent Transactions by Hour of Day ---
sns.countplot(x='hour_of_day', hue='is_fraud', data=df, ax=axes[1])
axes[1].set_title('Transaction Volume by Hour', fontsize=14, weight='bold')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Hour of Day', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Number of Transactions', fontsize=12)
axes[1].legend(title='Is Fraud', labels=['No', 'Yes'])

# --- Plot 3: Count of Fraudulent Transactions by Transaction Type ---
sns.countplot(y='transaction_type', hue='is_fraud', data=df, ax=axes[2], order=df['transaction_type'].value_counts().index)
axes[2].set_title('Transaction Volume by Type', fontsize=14, weight='bold')
axes[2].set_xlabel('Number of Transactions', fontsize=12)
axes[2].set_ylabel('Transaction Type', fontsize=12)
axes[2].legend(title='Is Fraud', labels=['No', 'Yes'])

# Add a comprehensive main title to the figure
fig.suptitle('Analysis of Fraudulent Transactions', fontsize=18, weight='bold')

# Adjust layout to prevent titles and labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95])

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
